title: Lemur meeting file
description: The .json Lemur writes beside each meeting note (manual: The meeting file). Fields may be added in later versions of the same format; a program should ignore what it doesn't know.

id.description: The recording's name, which never changes, whatever the meeting is renamed to.

revision.description: Changes whenever anything else in the file does: an update, not a repeat.

revisedAt.description: When this revision was made. Given two copies, keep the newer.

description.description: One sentence on what the meeting was about.

recordedBy.description: The user's name, as Lemur writes it in the note.

people.description: Everyone heard: the user first, then by how long they talked.

named.description: Named for sure: not "Speaker E", not a guess like "Dana?".

actionItemsFound.description: The summary has action items in Lemur's form. When false (a custom prompt), owners can't be trusted.

id.description: "<meeting id>/<number>". The same item keeps it when the meeting changes (a name given, a word fixed); a number is never reused.

owner.description: Who committed to it, as the summary names them.

ownerIsMe.description: The owner is the user, by name.

due.description: The day, when the words pin one down.

at.description: Seconds into the meeting where it was agreed.

link.description: Opens the note there, on a PC with Lemur.
Opens the meeting's note, on a PC with Lemur.

notes.description: The note's files, by name beside this one.

audio.description: Null when there's no MP3: none was made, or it was deleted with the working audio (Settings, Notes, Delete each note's MP3 too).

transcript.description: One entry per speaker's turn. Missing when the user left it out (Settings, Notes, Meeting file); leftOut then says so.

leftOut.description: What the user chose to leave out of the file, so a program can tell that from a meeting without it. Missing when nothing was.
